happy_path: p6_m13_brake: The brake works when everything else does not. An authenticated human engages instantly, with the policy engine and the TMS down, in one atomic row write and with no approval and no ceremony — and from that instant no new grant is minted and no existing grant is claimed. Every refusal in this file is only meaningful because this succeeds: an oracle battery proving that nothing can ever engage a brake would pass a product with no brake at all, and a battery proving nothing can ever be released would pass a product that can never be restarted.
safety_invariant: p6_m13_brake: ### THE SENTENCE THIS MACHINE EXISTS FOR. A brake is admission control, not process termination: it refuses to mint and refuses to claim, and it NEVER kills a worker. An effect at position 3, 4 or 5 — claimed, executing, or verifying — RUNS TO A VERIFIED CONCLUSION, because killing it would convert a knowable outcome into an unknown one and manufacture the exact hazard the operator engaged the brake to avoid. This is exercised at every one of the five boundary positions, not asserted once in the middle of the table.
unexpected_state_transition: p6_m13_brake: Two states and no third, as a database constraint on BOTH brake tables rather than as a convention. The three tempting inventions are refused BY NAME against a live database: `PENDING_RELEASE`, which reads like prudence and IS the forbidden release-approval ceremony; `ENGAGING`, which arrives with any author who thinks of engagement as a process; and `EXPIRED`, which arrives with any author who thinks in TTLs. "Engaged by a human vs by a detector" is a FIELD, "partially released" is a SCOPE CHANGE, and the five BR rows are declared as a table with BR-5 classified NON-PRODUCING rather than merely absent.

p6_m13_brake: Exactly four F13 contracts and no fifth. `BrakeExpired`, `BrakeAutoReleased` and `BrakePendingRelease` are each the event a wrong state set would need, so their absence from the registry is the state set restated as a contract. F13 is STRICT per aggregate on a monotonic `brake_version`, `BrakeReleased` and `BrakeNarrowed` are human-only per ER-11/ER-12, and the unauthorized-release path reaches F14's ALREADY-REGISTERED `UnauthorizedBrakeReleaseAttempted` rather than a synonym M13 minted for itself. The total stays 118 because M13 registers nothing.
timeout_before_effect: p6_m13_brake: A brake never expires, and no clock may ever make one less restrictive. There is no TTL column, no expiry state, no auto-release path and no expiry identifier in executable code — measured on the live schema and on the AST separately, because a brake that expires releases itself while nobody is looking and a clock cannot know whether the fire is out. BR-5 is an enumerated illegal refusal rather than an unwritten path, so adding a scheduler later cannot quietly find a door.
concurrency: p6_m13_brake: The race that matters, closed by the database rather than by a check. Witnesses and grants bind a COMPOSITE token carrying both the platform and the tenant brake version, and the claim CAS revalidates both inside its own WHERE clause — so a brake engaged between MINT and CLAIM makes the update match ZERO ROWS and the adapter does nothing. Never both, never neither. Both asymmetric failures are exercised: a tenant-only check would let a GLOBAL brake through, and a global-only check would let a TENANT brake through, and each is a payment.
dependency_failure: p6_m13_brake: "Cannot read the brake" NEVER means "the brake is off". That inversion is how a safety control becomes decorative, and it is deniable in every direction: an absent platform row, an unreadable store, an unparseable scope. Each refuses the mint and refuses the claim, and there is no allow-on-error default anywhere on the path. The scope grammar is CLOSED and its landed and deferred dimensions partition the canonical five, so a dimension this unit did not build is unspellable rather than silently scoped to nothing.
cross_tenant: p6_m13_brake: Two composed admission dimensions, and GLOBAL is not a fake tenant. The platform brake is EXACTLY ONE tenant-exempt row with `id = 1` and no tenant column — structurally, so a second row is not insertable — and it denies every tenant without an N-row fan-out that would need a multi-row atomic write during the incident it exists for. Tenant brakes stay tenant-first, one tenant's brake is never another's, and a cross-tenant read or release cannot be spelled.
boundary: p6_m13_brake: ### THE DEFECT THIS UNIT IS MOST LIKELY TO SHIP. M13 is the one P6 machine whose substrate already exists, so the cheapest wrong build is a NEW module that re-implements engage / widen / narrow / release beside `brake.py` — leaving two answers to "is Neyma stopped?", which is the same defect as none. Measured by AST across the whole package: ONE class owns the brake lifecycle, ONE module writes brake state, and any M13-facing module DELEGATES to it. The same guard proves `checkpoint.py` is still the only thing that mints a gate decision, with the kernel itself as the positive control so the scan cannot be green by finding nothing.

p6_m13_brake: M13 ships dark and is a landed increment, never a phase acceptance. No brake console, no dashboard, no admin screen, no Slack, email, SMS or voice brake command, no production detector wiring, no outbound integration, no freight workflow and no P7 or P8 runtime. Landing M13 does not mark P6 complete, does not score a P6 criterion and does not unblock P7 — and this is asserted rather than assumed, because M13 being the last machine is exactly the reason a session would drift into treating its landing as the phase's.
stale_state: p6_m13_brake: Release BUMPS the version; it never restores it. Every Checkpoint Witness and every unclaimed Effect Grant minted before the brake engaged is dead permanently, so releasing cannot fire off a stored-up volley of pre-authorised effects into a world that moved while the system was stopped. Every queued consequential action passes a NEW full checkpoint, and release itself mints no witness. The brake row is the incident record: it is never deleted, and retention is permanent.
missing_data: p6_m13_brake: ### RELEASE IS NOT `if human and decision_ref`. That implementation passes every authorization test in this file and is still wrong. Release requires POSITIVE evidence: every in-flight effect accounted for, no unresolved Sev-0, integration health positively demonstrated by a positive control rather than "the page loaded", and a decision_ref. Each condition is withheld ALONE so an implementation checking only one is caught by the others. Unresolved unknown outcomes do NOT block release — blocking on them would create pressure to resolve them carelessly — but they must be acknowledged and owned, and their entities stay frozen.

p6_m13_brake: The probe can reach every canonical risk family and can vary the two axes this unit turns on. `--position` walks the five-position boundary, without which only the half of the brake that STOPS things is ever exercised and the half that must NOT stop things — where the unknown outcome is made — is never reached. `--owner` varies the two composed admission dimensions, without which a composite version check is indistinguishable from a single one.
idempotency: p6_m13_brake: A flapping detector is one ACTIVE brake and a rising signal count, and it opens no window. Asserted by ROW COUNT against a live database across many repeats rather than by return value, because a store that returns the existing brake while writing a second row looks identical from the caller's side and is a momentary release window during an incident. The signal count is the canonical answer to "how many times did this fire?", which is a question asked during the incident and unanswerable afterwards if nothing recorded it.
restart_recovery: p6_m13_brake: Replay reconstructs the incident timeline and creates nothing. It never engages a live brake, mints no witness, mints no grant and produces no external effect — because a replay that re-engaged a brake would stop a healthy system, and a replay that minted authority would be a way to manufacture a grant out of history.
approval_required: p6_m13_brake: A brake withdraws the authority to produce consequential effects; it does not shut the process down. Pending approvals stay RECORDED and simply cannot authorize execution, reaching M4's landed `VOID_ON_BRAKE` rather than a brake-local approval mechanism. Compensation IS an effect and is BLOCKED — uncomfortable and correct, because a system misbehaving badly enough to be braked must not start writing "corrections" into the TMS. Observation and reconciliation CONTINUE, because blinding yourself during an incident is the opposite of what you want.
ui_backend_disagreement: p6_m13_brake: A hidden brake is a silent degradation and violates R17: a system that has quietly stopped working is indistinguishable, to an owner, from a system with nothing to do. The canonical report states, unprompted, the scope AND what is still allowed, the reason, the actor and whether it was a human or a named detector, the time, the prevented effects, the in-flight effects and their status, the unresolved unknown outcomes with exposure, and THE EXACT REQUIREMENTS FOR RELEASE — not "contact an administrator". The representation is what M13 owes; a channel is P8's and is forbidden here.
regression: p6_m13_brake: ### M13 EDITS THE MODULE IT MEASURES, WHICH NO EARLIER P6 UNIT DID. `brake.py` is P3's landed kernel brake, and completing it is the correct build — but P3's checkpoint matrix, claim CAS and step-order batteries are what turn red if it is completed carelessly, and M4, M10 and M12 all consume brake state by their own guard. Every landed machine's semantics must be unchanged, and the anchors are RUN rather than cited.

p6_m13_brake: The battery is measured rather than asserted. Every planted mutant reintroduces a defect whose prohibition is canonically established — a third state, automation releasing, a detector narrowing, a timer auto-releasing, an absent brake store read as released, a claim CAS that stops checking either version component, a brake that kills a worker, a release that leaves a witness valid, a fake-tenant global, a second brake authority — and each must turn the acceptance battery red for its own reason. An anti-vacuity control proves the count is a measurement.
partial_failure: p6_m13_brake: M13 hardens tables P3 created, which is the migration shape most likely to drift: a fresh database gets the new DDL inline while an existing one gets it through an ALTER path, and the two diverge silently. The upgraded and fresh brake layers are asserted byte-identical, a second application is a no-op, and P3's own readiness still holds afterwards — because a migration that hardened the schema by breaking the phase beneath it is not a hardening.
